answers.question: Which experiments are relevant to smoke detection, and what particle sizes did they measure?
answers.answer:
Experiments relevant to smoke detection include:
- [PSI-101] SAME-R: Measured particle sizes ranging from 100 to 600 nm, increasing substantially with aging and decreasing air flow [ntrs:20140006585].
- [PSI-102] SAME: Measured smoke particle sizes typically 50% larger in count mean diameter in low-gravity compared to normal gravity, with resultant sizes below 300 nm [ntrs:20080012612, PSI-102].

answers.question: Which materials were burned in Saffire-II and what was learned?
answers.answer:
In SAFFIRE-II [PSI-99], the following materials were burned:
- PMMA (polymethyl methacrylate)
- Nomex
- SIBAL
- Silicone
- Composite fabric (75% cotton – 25% fiberglass by mass)

The experiment determined microgravity flammability limits for these materials [PSI-99, ntrs:20170001636]. It also validated NASA's material selection criteria [PSI-99, ntrs:20200000557].

answers.question: What is a cool flame and which experiments observed one?
answers.answer:
A cool flame is defined as low-temperature oxidation with almost no visible emission, which can persist after the hot flame goes out, posing a re-ignition risk [glossary]. Several experiments observed cool flames:

- [PSI-39] CFI observed cool flames and analyzed their behavior under helium dilution [PSI-39].
- [PSI-10] ACME/Flame Design experiment also observed cool flames, as part of its combustion tests [PSI-10].

passages.text: Glossary, LUCI / FM2: Planned partial-gravity combustion tests. No data in PSI yet.

ACME CLD Flame (PSI-21), PSI objectives: In order to provide the experimental data needed to allow rigorous testing of computational models at the extremes of the fuel dilution spectrum, we have the following objectives:
FLEX (PSI-69), test condition (flight): LOI tests at varying pressures and oxygen concentrations. Evidence: Select the test pressure (0.5 − 1.5 atm) for the LOI tests.

SAFFIRE-II (PSI-99), finding of the paper "The Spacecraft Fire Experiment (Saffire) - Objectives, Development and Status": The selected materials have normal gravity Maximum Oxygen Concentration (MOC) flammability limits that indicate they will burn in normal gravity just above and below 21% O2 by volume.

FLEX (PSI-69), test condition (flight): n-decane droplets, 0.5 atm pressure, 21% O2 and 79% N2. Evidence: Figure 1a (R377) corresponds to a n-decane droplet with an initial diameter of 4.03 mm burning in 21% oxygen and 79% nitrogen mixture at 0.5 atm pressure.

FLEX (PSI-69), test condition (flight): n-decane droplets, 0.5 atm pressure, 25% O2 and 75% N2. Evidence: Figure 1b (R374) shows the combustion characteristics for a 3.79 mm n-decane droplet burning at a slightly increased oxygen concentration of 25% and the rest being nitrogen at 0.5 atm pressure.
Glossary, Cygnus: Cargo spacecraft. Saffire ran after it undocked from the ISS, with no risk to the crew.

BASS-II (PSI-25), finding of the paper "Correlation of Normal Gravity Mixed Convection Blowoff Limits with Microgravity Forced Flow Blowoff Limits": Each boundary is approximately linear with flow, with the exception of the 14% oxygen data.

SAFFIRE-III (PSI-100), PSI objectives: (1) determine how rapidly a large scale fire grows in low-gravity and (2) investigate the low-g flammability limits compared to those obtained in NASA’s normal gravity material flammability screening test.
